correctness.rationale: For any selected blade vertex the exact inequality is 2(k_i-1+z0)+1 >= r_i; with no hub every occupied blade requires a_i+1 vertices, and global minimality forces one tight blade. With hub the local threshold is a_i and the center requires K>=floor(R/2)=T+floor(o/2). A blade count above a_i would contain a non-hub suballiance, so K<=T and o<=1, with all blade counts tight. Proper subsets then fail either the center or peripheral inequality. Independent exhaustive graph-definition checks cover 21 cases (18,891 input subsets). The proof, not enumeration, establishes all parameter values.

value.rationale: The 2023 minimal defensive-alliance enumeration literature motivates natural structural families in which every globally minimal solution can be counted. This classification determines every solution and all cardinality multiplicities for heterogeneous clique bouquets, finds a sharp odd-blade parity obstruction to center-containing solutions, and constructs an unbounded minimum-to-upper globally minimal size gap in a canonical graph family. These facts depend on globally minimal suballiance exclusion and are not a mere graph-parameter substitution, isolated numerology, or straightforward consequence of an existing polynomial.
